title: Move the Cassano Shellys to the IoT network

blocks.title: Yes, it is possible
blocks.content: All 14 Shellys at Cassano can move from the office network (Default) to the IoT network. Home Assistant can already reach the IoT network: I tested it today, 0% loss, about 9 ms. 5 of the 14 Shellys already work there. Cost: 0 euro. Effort: about 2 hours of my time, in 4 short waves. Best moment: now, because heating and cooling are off.

payload.headline: Yes. All 14 Shellys can move to IoT. Cost 0 euro, about 2 hours.
payload.summary: Home Assistant already controls 5 Shellys on IoT without problems. No firewall rule blocks the move. The only risk is a few minutes without control per wave, and that matters only when heating or cooling is on.
payload.affected: Fancoils, chiller master, shades and wall displays. Nobody notices while the season is off.

blocks.title: What changes
blocks.content: Before: 9 Shellys sit on the office network, next to PCs and the NAS. After: all Shellys sit on IoT. The firewall then stops a hacked or buggy Shelly from reaching office PCs and the NAS. Home Assistant still controls them, because office-to-IoT traffic is allowed.

blocks.title: The 4 waves
blocks.content: Each wave: reserve the new address, switch the network, restart the Shelly, check Home Assistant sees it, else roll back to the office network in 1 minute.

Wave 3: 7 Shellys on the shared port

scenarios.label: Shared port fails
scenarios.summary: I set the port back to the office network and restart the 7 Shellys. Stepless fancoils and Mensa shades are back in about 2 minutes.

blocks.title: Decision: move all 14 Shellys to IoT, in 4 waves, starting today while the season is off
blocks.content: I move all 14, one wave at a time, with a check and a 1-minute rollback after each. The chiller master goes last and only while the chiller has been off for at least 10 minutes. Reject means: I move only the Mensa wall display (Wi-Fi, easy) and leave the 9 wired Shellys on the office network.

payload.summary: All 14 to IoT, 4 waves, starting today.
payload.consequence: Each wave can drop control of its devices for about 2 minutes. While the season is off, nothing heats or cools, so nobody notices. One step needs a person: someone picks the ff4.iot Wi-Fi on the Mensa wall display screen (I tell you when).

blocks.title: How I do it (technical)
blocks.content:
Facts: docs/investigations/2026-10-13-shelly-iot-move-facts.md. All 14 are Gen2, mains, DHCP. No outbound websocket, MQTT, CoIoT, webhooks or scripts, so the IoT-to-office block breaks nothing. Shelly Cloud stays working (IoT has internet).

1. Before each wave: UniFi DHCP reservation on IoT per MAC. Old Default reservations (.41 .42 .51) removed after.
2. Wired: set the UniFi port native network to IoT. Ent48 port 2 feeds an unmanaged switch with 7 Shellys, so a port bounce does NOT renew their DHCP. Fix: Shelly.Reboot with delay_ms 60000 to all 7 first, then change the port inside that minute. Same reboot trick for the single ports (UDM 5, Rack Top 19 and 23); there is no PoE to cycle.
3. Dual-homed (34987a, 963420, 971434): after the cable is on IoT, turn their Wi-Fi off, so each has one address.
4. Home Assistant: Shelly zeroconf should update the stored host (mDNS is reflected across networks). If an entry keeps the old host, use the reconfigure flow (a plain reload does not help, Morazzone lesson).
5. eaf568 (chiller): switch_2 boots as match_input, so a reboot leaves the chiller off. Do it only with season off and chiller off >= 10 min. ea3fc4 outputs 1 and 3 now boot ON; Home Assistant turns them off again while the season is off.
6. Verify per wave: every Shelly entity available in HA, UniFi shows the client on IoT with the reserved IP, one switch toggle test on a non-critical output.
7. Rollback: port back to Default plus reboot (wired), or re-join ff4.wifi (display).
